EagleRock: $15.4 Million Midland Basin Acquisitions And Double Eagle V Agreement Expand Permian Footprint
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 3:45 PM
EagleRock: $15.4 Million Midland Basin Acquisitions And Double Eagle V Agreement Expand Permian Footprint
EagleRock has completed two acquisitions in the Midland Basin for a combined $15.4 million and entered into an agreement with Double Eagle V covering approximately 35,000 additional dedicated acres. The transactions expand EagleRock’s surface land and infrastructure operations in the Permian Basin while increasing its exposure to water management and royalty revenue opportunities.
The additional acreage dedication increases the land dedicated to EagleRock by Double Eagle in the Midland Basin to approximately 105,000 acres.
The new agreement covers approximately 35,000 acres across Midland and Glasscock counties in Texas.
It represents an increase of approximately 50% in Double Eagle’s dedicated acreage within the region.
EagleRock expects the agreement to generate additional royalty revenue without requiring an upfront capital investment.
This structure reflects the company’s capital-light operating model, which uses agreements with energy producers to generate income from the use of surface land and associated infrastructure.
Double Eagle V is an active private operator in the Midland Basin and EagleRock’s largest shareholder.
The additional dedication strengthens the relationship between the two companies and provides EagleRock with exposure to future development activity.
Management expects the agreement to begin making a meaningful revenue contribution in 2027.
Additional growth could follow as Double Eagle advances drilling and completion activities across the dedicated acreage.
Alongside the agreement, EagleRock acquired two properties totaling approximately 2,000 acres.
The acquisitions were completed at an aggregate price of $15.4 million.
EagleRock financed the purchases through cash on hand and borrowings under its existing revolving credit facility.
The company said the assets were purchased at a valuation below 10 times EBITDA.
One property is located directly adjacent to EagleRock’s existing Shallow Valley operations.
The other is adjacent to the newly announced Double Eagle V acreage dedication.
The geographic proximity is intended to support operational coordination and improve the company’s ability to serve customers.
The acquired properties provide additional water supply, storage, and disposal capabilities.
They also include potential opportunities for sand development.
These assets can support oil and gas operators that require water management services and access to infrastructure during drilling and production.
Water handling is a significant operational requirement in the Permian Basin because energy development involves both water consumption and the management of produced water.
Companies providing surface land and related infrastructure can participate in these activities through leases, royalties, and service arrangements.
EagleRock believes the acquisitions will create opportunities to increase revenue while benefiting from shared operating capabilities.
Following the transactions, the company’s Midland Basin portfolio includes approximately 44,000 acres of controlled surface land and approximately 105,000 dedicated acres.
The larger footprint provides additional exposure to energy development across the region.

CSIRO spinout lands $15 million to make green hydrogen using less power
Hadean grabs $15m to turn factory waste heat into cheaper green hydrogen for steel. Watch this pilot test the hydrogen hype.
Simon Thomsen
Nov 9, 2026
2 min read
Share
0
Prefer Startup Daily
The Hadean Energy team
CSIRO spinout Hadean Energy has secured a $15 million grant from the Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) to test whether waste heat from heavy industry can cut the cost of making green hydrogen.
ARENA will fund half the $30 million pilot plant proposed for industrial gas supplier BOC’s Western Port site in Victoria. The plant will produce up to 7kg of hydrogen hourly for a neighbouring steelworks. That’s about 85% of the hydrogen needed for annealing, a heat treatment to prevent the steel’s surface from oxidising.
CSIRO and corporate adviser RFC Ambrian launched Hadean in 2023, with the latter’s fund dropping $1.5 million into its seed round that year.
Based at CSIRO’s Clayton research precinct in Melbourne, Hadean is commercialising a tubular solid oxide electrolyser researchers spent eight years developing. Its ceramic tubes use electricity and heat to split steam into hydrogen and oxygen. Hadean estimates that tapping the heat a factory already generates can reduce electricity use by around 30% compared to conventional electrolysers.
In 2024, a prototype ran for 1,000 hours at BlueScope’s Port Kembla steelworks in NSW. It used less than 36 kilowatt-hours of electricity per kilogram of hydrogen by using steam from the plant. The Victorian pilot will scale the system from about one kilowatt to 200-300kW.

ARENA CEO Darren Miller said green hydrogen has significant potential to reduce emissions from industries that are difficult to electrify.
“This pilot will demonstrate how Hadean’s technology performs in a real-world industrial environment and provide the evidence needed to assess its commercial potential,” he said.
“This could open the door to broader use of green hydrogen in steelmaking and other industrial applications, while helping build Australia’s hydrogen industrial capability.”
Hadean also raised capital from RFC Ambrian, engineering partner Amarna Energy and private investors to cover its share of the initial design and engineering work. Amarna will design the equipment that connects the electrolyser to industrial sites.
The startup expects to raise more capital over the next 12 months for construction costs.
